extracted.intended_audience: State air agency staff (permit writers), EPA regional reviewers, regulated electric generating unit owners/operators, environmental attorneys, and public commenters on SIP/RACT permit revisions
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating whether state-submitted case-by-case RACT (reasonably available control technology) permit limits and supporting materials satisfy the Clean Air Act, applicable case law (e.g., Sierra Club v. EPA), EPA policy (including SSM policy), and are enforceable as SIP provisions. Includes checking technical justification, data analysis, enforceability, monitoring/reporting, and non-interference with attainment (CAA 110(l)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of RACT requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The RACT requirements in CAA section 182(b)(2) apply to all ozone nonattainment areas classified as Moderate or higher; section 184(b)(1)(B) applies RACT to areas located within ozone transport regions. The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is part of the Ozone Transport Region and therefore subject statewide to RACT requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the geographic and statutory applicability of RACT (which NAAQS, which areas, which major sources) and ensure the SIP submission addresses the correct NAAQS and sources. Identify whether the submission intentionally excludes other NAAQS (e.g., 2015) and ensure that is documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate justification of RACT limits (technology-forcing / legal standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SIP must justify the selection of permit limits as RACT consistent with applicable requirements and case law. Following Sierra Club v. EPA, the new standard (SIP or FIP) “must be technology forcing, in accord with [EPA's] RACT standard, and lack the gaping loophole found in the [2016 SIP's] enforcement regime.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a reasoned explanation showing why selected limits reflect RACT (not merely historical average emissions), why lower achievable limits are infeasible if claimed, and explain why the limit is appropriately technology-forcing. Cite and apply relevant case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and demonstration of lowest achievable emission rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should identify the lowest achievable NOx emission rate (or explain how the selected rate relates to the lowest achievable) and explain how other operating factors affect that rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the empirical minimum emission rates observed, describe the conditions under which lower rates were achieved, and explicitly explain why those lower rates are not the basis for the RACT limit (if they are not). Avoid relying solely on averages of historical emissions without explaining infeasibility of lower rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent data, methods, and time frame for analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The SIP/technical evaluation memos must state the data sources, years and months analyzed (e.g., CAMD database years), and the methodology used to derive limits (e.g., top-down approach, load-specific analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete, reproducible descriptions of datasets (which years/months), analyses (how daily averages, setpoints, reagent vs. heat input were analyzed), plots/figures used, and any assumptions. Resolve inconsistencies (e.g., different years referenced in TEM vs. RTC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of alternative controls and cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: PADEP used EPA Control Cost Manual and vendor quotes to determine whether identified control options were technically feasible and cost effective, and evaluated multiple NOx control technologies (precombustion, combustion, post‑combustion, station‑wide improvements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the list of controls considered, technical feasibility analysis, cost estimates (with sources), and explain why additional controls beyond those relied on (e.g., tuning or SCR optimization) are not cost-effective or feasible. Include vendor quotes, Control Cost Manual calculations, and rationale for ruling out options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceability and clear objective criteria for when limits apply (SCR‑on applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits must set forth clear, objective criteria for determining when emissions are subject to an SCR-on lb/MMBtu daily average limit; otherwise EPA/public cannot determine applicability or enforce noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define in the permit the conditions (e.g., SCR operating state, temperature thresholds, setpoint definitions) that trigger the SCR‑on limit, provide objective metrics and monitoring parameters so EPA and the public can determine applicability, and avoid vague or post‑hoc determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unbounded director's discretion and post‑hoc exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: SIP/permits must not include unbounded director discretion allowing exemptions during startup/shutdown/emergency/technically infeasible periods; such post‑hoc determinations are the type of director's discretion prohibited by the CAA and EPA SSM policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid permitting language that allows the director to exclude emissions from calculations without defined, bounded criteria and a transparent process. If any discretionary determinations are included, provide clear procedural safeguards, explicit factors, and documentation requirements that are publicly accessible and not arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with EPA SSM policy (startup, shutdown, malfunction)
rubrics_metrics.description: SIP provisions must be consistent with EPA's restated SSM policy applicable to SIPs; provisions that allow excess emissions during SSM without enforceable limits or clear conditions are problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure SSM exclusions are narrowly defined, justified, and that the SIP provides enforceable requirements (work practices, monitoring) to limit excess emissions. Do not include broad carve-outs for SSM or similar events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and bounding of emergency operation exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions such as 'operation pursuant to emergency generation required by PJM' must be defined and bounded in the permit, including what constitutes technical infeasibility and how such demonstrations are made and reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define terms (e.g., 'operation pursuant to emergency generation required by PJM'), list the factors that may lead to technical infeasibility, provide the process and criteria for demonstrations, and specify who reviews/approves and how the public/EPA can verify the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping sufficient to determine compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits (and unredacted SIP submittals) should require monthly reports (or other reporting) that include hourly load levels, heat input, ammonia injection rates, NOx rates, total NOx emissions, SCR emission set point, SCR inlet and outlet temperature, and detailed hourly data and explanations for days exceeding SCR-on limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require continuous monitoring and retention of necessary parameters, prescribe the reporting frequency and level of detail (hourly where needed), and ensure reports are adequate for the public and EPA to verify compliance and applicability determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification and derivation of all‑conditions 30‑day rolling lb/hr limits
rubrics_metrics.description: 30‑day rolling average pounds/hr limits must be explicitly derived and justified (e.g., whether derived from SCR-on lb/MMBtu × rated MMBtu/hr, or from observed 30‑day rolling lb/hr CAMD data) and shown to act as a constraint on operation without SCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear calculations or analyses showing how mass‑based limits were developed, the relationship to lb/MMBtu limits, and demonstrate that the 30‑day limit will constrain operation during periods when SCR is unavailable (i.e., will force more SCR use or lower load), with supporting dataset/figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for compliance buffers and their magnitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: If a compliance 'buffer' (margin) is added to calculated limits (e.g., 10–21% above rate at capacity), the SIP must explain why such buffers are necessary, technologically and economically feasible, and why buffers differ across units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify and justify buffers with analysis (variability, uncertainty, operational margins), explain necessity, and avoid arbitrary or unexplained percentage additions. Provide unit‑specific rationale when buffers vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of operational loopholes tied to arbitrary thresholds (e.g., SCR inlet temperature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards should not create loopholes that permit unlimited operation without SCR controls if operators maintain parameters (like SCR inlet temperature) below an arbitrary threshold; reporting of such parameters must be enforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If limits are tied to thresholds (e.g., 600°F inlet temperature), require continuous monitoring and reporting of the parameter, explain the technical basis for the threshold, and ensure the threshold cannot be used as a loophole to avoid controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification that limits will not increase emissions (CAA section 110(l) non‑interference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 110(l) prohibits approving a SIP revision if it would interfere with attainment or reasonable further progress. EPA has interpreted this as permitting approval so long as 'emissions in the air are not increased.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an analysis demonstrating that approval will not cause increased air emissions or interfere with attainment/maintenance obligations; consider the particular ways a SIP revision could interfere and analyze variables specific to the revision rather than relying on a generic test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and reconciliation between supporting documents (TEMs, RTCs, permits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting documents (Technical Evaluation Memos, Responses to Comments, permits) must be consistent (e.g., same years of data, same derivation methods) and any discrepancies must be explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross‑check TEMs, RTCs, and permit language for consistency. Where differences exist (e.g., years analyzed, methods used), explain and document reasons. Ensure the public SIP submittal includes complete, unredacted permits and accompanying memos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration that the chosen operational measures (e.g., boiler tuning) yield projected reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the SIP relies on operational changes (e.g., boiler 'tuning') rather than physical add‑ons, the submission must quantify expected NOx reductions (e.g., 5–15% or an average of 10%) and document the basis for those estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide empirical support (studies, site demonstrations, historical data) showing tuning will achieve the claimed reductions, describe required work practices, inspection and maintenance, and include enforceable work practice conditions and verification procedures.
